crime: Carrying her newborn brother down the stairs, {WITCH_NAME} pictured opening her arms. She sat down on the step and held him until her mother came. Her mother took him and never let her hold him again.

One girl couldn't sleep in her dark, locked cell. Every afternoon she napped under the unwilting cherry tree in the library with her head on {WITCH_NAME}'s lap. Whenever the girl stirred, {WITCH_NAME} stopped time with her Magic and stood over her, staring at her own hands, thinking that a girl who could picture what they might do was a girl who would do it.

At half past one, the girl drew {WITCH_NAME}'s palm down over her eyes. "Every afternoon," she said, "until they let us out." {WITCH_NAME} did not wait to find out. She slid her palm down over the girl's nose and mouth and pressed her face into the skirt over her lap until she was still. At ten to two, she laid the girl on the bench as if asleep and joined the girls at the pool table in the recreation room.

At twenty to three, the prisoners heard a body fall in the library while {WITCH_NAME} was lining up a shot beside them. They found the girl dead on the floor below the bench, fingertip bruises along her jaw. In the trial court, they ruled that she had been held down and had fallen at twenty to three, while {WITCH_NAME} stood at the pool table with them.

But one prisoner had turned the dead girl's face and found the weave of {WITCH_NAME}'s skirt still sharp on her cheek, an hour after {WITCH_NAME} had risen: a crease living skin would have lost. The girl had died in that lap at half past one. At twenty to three, from the pool table, {WITCH_NAME} had stopped time, gone back to the library and left the body hanging upright in the air beside the bench, to drop the instant time ran again.
fields.epitaph: At nine she held on. What she pictured was never what her hands did—until she stopped waiting to find out.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Never Trusted Her Own Hands
execution: A steep wooden staircase, the kind found in a house, rises high above the floor of the trial court. Its treads are worn hollow in the middle. She is swaddled from ankles to chin in a vast white baby blanket, not a finger free, and laid across the top step. The staircase tips her off, and she tumbles down, step after step. She watches each step come, eyes open. She cannot sit down, and she has no arm free to hold on. At the foot of the stairs, the white bundle comes to rest and lies still.

magic.name: The Held Moment
magic.text: She can stop time for everything but herself.
